kernel_of_truth.description: The dome’s underlying intuition — that ancient cosmological texts treat the sky as a solid material — is historically defensible. Bronze Age Near Eastern cosmology did read the heavens as a metallic vault (e.g., Egyptian sky-as-iron-plate, Babylonian sky-as-marble), and the Hebrew רָקִיעַ (raqia) in Genesis 1:6-8 does carry a beaten-metal etymology in some lexicons. The dome model’s textual reading of Job 37:18 and Deut 28:23 (data/wins.json:WIN-034.detail_evidence) is not invented; biblical scholars Walton and Seely have both written defensible academic treatments of ancient Near Eastern solid-sky cosmology. The dome author isn’t hallucinating the textual layer.
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: The kernel buys ancient-cosmology textual scholarship — it does NOT buy a contemporary physical specification. Once the dome author elevates the metaphor to a load-bearing engineering premise (raw-text/05-model.txt:79-80) and uses it as evidence in WIN-029 (Schumann) and WIN-048 (CMB), the claim becomes testable. At that point the dome’s own published parameters (H(r)=8537·exp(−r/8619), per data/wins.json:WIN-038.detail_evidence pole-floor derivation) force the three-leg self-contradiction: copper at 1 GHz (skin depth ~2 μm) and 160 GHz (~0.16 μm) blocks radio astronomy and CMB observation, and the cavity it forms resonates at ~8.78 Hz not the observed 7.83 Hz. Walton and Seely are describing ancient cosmology as the ancients held it; the dome model is asserting it as the contemporary fact. The kernel survives as scholarship; the WIN does not survive as physics.
